provisional_claims.summary: Engine/calendar fixes: (1) season(day) was offset by one season (day 0 reported Highsummer; docs: day 0 is Dawn) — fixed in engine.season and weather_on wetness index so Highsummer stays driest; (2) calendar_day season_day was (day+1)%12+1, now day%12+1; (3) almanac longest_dry_spell counted drizzle days instead of clear (rainfall 0) days; (4) next_weather searched from today rather than future days; (5) calendar showed one extra plan occurrence (gap//repeat <= remaining → <); (6) neighbor moisture used partially-updated current-day cells instead of the start-of-day snapshot (garden should grow together); (7) plant comfort used base shade instead of effective shade from shade cloth; (8) plant death age hardcoded to 105 ignoring species lifespan (glowcap 75); (9) bare ground never recovered 1 nutrient/day; (10) Hush penalty applied to glowcaps which docs say remain suited.
provisional_claims.reproduction: from mosslight.engine import season; season(0) -> 'Highsummer' (expected Dawn). weather.calendar_day(0)['season_day'] -> 2 (expected 1). Plant glowcap aged 70 and step 10 days: not removed at lifespan 75. Bare tile nutrients stay constant across steps.

provisional_claims.summary: Habitat fixes: (1) effective_shade omitted the tile below (x, y+1), so shade cloth didn't shelter all adjoining tiles; (2) rain barrels added +6 moisture every day, docs/runtime say only on rainy days; (3) stress increased at vitality == 30, docs say below 30; (4) worms only counted soil, docs say moist rich soil or peat.
provisional_claims.reproduction: create(1,6,6); set_structure(w,2,2,'shade_cloth'); effective_shade(w, w.index(2,3)) == base shade (expected +15). Rain barrel on a clear day raises moisture by 6. Peat tiles with moisture>=45 nutrients>=40 yield no worms.

provisional_claims.summary: Notebook defects: (1) search_notes end date exclusive (should be inclusive range); (2) tag filter matched substrings of tags instead of exact tag; (3) press_specimen dropped vitality so specimen lacks measurement and save fails validation on reload; (4) complete_task ignored done=false (cannot reopen); (5) overdue tasks included today's tasks (should be due < today); (6) task lists sorted by id instead of earliest due date first.
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=create(3,8,6); step(w,30); add_task(w,'t',30); task_list(w,'overdue') contained the day-30 task; complete_task(w,1,False) left done=True; press_specimen then World.from_dict(w.to_dict()) raised 'vitality must be integer'; add_note(labels=['pondside']); search_notes(tag='pond') returned it; note from day==end excluded.

provisional_claims.summary: Nursery defects: watering added only one day instead of restoring the three-day supply; dry days still advanced batch age (development should halt); plant_out only deducted four nutrients for the final seedling of a batch instead of every seedling.
provisional_claims.reproduction: start_seeds, let hydration drop to 0 over 3 days, water_batch -> hydration was 1 (expected 3); a dry day incremented age; plant_out with count=2 left tile nutrients unchanged.

provisional_claims.summary: Gardening defects: rectangle() excluded the right column (inclusive rectangle expected); circle brush used diamond (Manhattan) distance; transplant discarded stress instead of carrying it to the destination; prune could make age negative and vitality exceed 100; craft only checked single-unit cost, allowing negative inventory for amount>1.
provisional_claims.reproduction: rectangle(w,0,0,2,1) returned 4 tiles (expected 6); brush(w,5,5,2,'circle') == diamond; transplant tile with stress 20 -> destination stress 0; prune age-3 plant -> age -2; inventory fiber=3, craft('compost',2) -> fiber -3.

provisional_claims.summary: Experiment defects: treatment events re-executed on every later offset (offset <= instead of ==); duplicate-name check was case-sensitive though names are stored casefolded ("Control" accepted); final observation omitted when days not divisible by every; against_control deltas computed backwards (control minus treatment).
provisional_claims.reproduction: experiment(w,5,[{"name":"W","events":[{"offset":1,"command":{"op":"tend","args":{"x":0,"y":0,"action":"water"}}}]}],every=2): water applied 5 times; samples at offsets 0,2,4 only (missing 5); treatment named "Control" accepted; planting treatment shows negative population_delta.

provisional_claims.summary: Planning fixes: (1) schedule rejected tomorrow (min day was world.day+2); docs: plans require a future first day (world.day+1 allowed); (2) add_bed name uniqueness was case-sensitive while save validation casefolds names, so "Fern" and "fern" produced an unloadable save; (3) run_rules evaluated conditions sequentially after earlier rules acted (rule 2 saw rule 1's watering). Rules now evaluate all conditions against the post-growth state before applying actions, per "Rules respond to the day's growing conditions consistently".
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=create(1,6,6); schedule(w,'p',w.day+1,[[0,0]],'water') raised ValueError. add_bed(w,'Fern',[[0,0]]); add_bed(w,'fern',[[1,1]]) succeeded then World.from_dict(w.to_dict()) fails. Two rules below 50 moisture on same tile with water: second rule skipped after first watered.

provisional_claims.summary: Analysis fixes: (1) census vitality average divided by all tiles instead of living plants; (2) diversity used log2 instead of natural log (docs: Shannon entropy with natural logarithms); (3) suitability ignored structure shelter (used base shade; imported effective_shade unused); (4) recommendations ignored empty_only=False and always omitted occupied ground; (5) forecast omitted the final day when days not divisible by every (docs: 10/3 samples 0,3,6,9,10).
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=create(34,8,6); census(w)['averages']['vitality'] was diluted by empty tiles; forecast(w,10,3) timeline days lacked final day; recommendations(w,'moss',100,False) same length as empty_only=True; shade cloth on tile did not change suitability effective_shade.

provisional_claims.summary: Exchange/model/state/commands defects: blueprint mirror and quarter-turn transforms were off by one (x=width-x, height-y) producing out-of-range coordinates; import_csv incremented revision twice; model accepted empty cells with age or vitality (and-vs-or); to_dict shared journal entry dicts with the live world (not independently editable); state validation allowed ids equal to next_id and plants on stone; execute accepted commands with keys other than op/args.
provisional_claims.reproduction: transform_blueprint(blueprint(w,0,0,2,1),mirror=True) -> tile x=3 invalid (validate_blueprint rejects); World.from_dict with cell {species:None, age:3, vitality:0} accepted; d=w.to_dict(); d['journal'][0]['text']='x' mutated w.journal; save with stone tile holding moss loaded; execute(w,{"op":"prune","args":{},"extra":1}) accepted.

provisional_claims.summary: Model/state/render/chart fixes: (1) World.to_dict journal was a shallow list, so editing returned journal entries mutated the original (docs: to_dict is independently editable); (2) save validation accepted empty cells with age but no vitality (used 'and' instead of 'or'); (3) workbench validation accepted identifiers equal to next_id (would duplicate the next created ID); (4) validation allowed plants on stone (only pond checked); (5) shade map layer showed base shade, docs say shade maps include structure shelter; (6) history chart placed points by index not actual day; (7) non-interactive SVG art tiles carried tabindex/role button attributes (example SVGs show them only when interactive).
provisional_claims.reproduction: d=w.to_dict(); d['journal'][0]['text']='x' changed w.journal. from_dict with empty cell age=5 vitality=0 accepted. Save with note id == next_id accepted. Save with stone tile containing moss accepted. render_map(w,'shade') ignores shade_cloth. render_history with history days [5,50] spaced evenly by index.

provisional_claims.summary: Care plans never advance: run_plans keeps a stale reference to the plan entry after tend_many replaces world.__dict__ (new workbench), so remaining/day/status updates are lost and the plan stays pending forever. Fixed by re-finding the entry after tend_many.
provisional_claims.reproduction: create(34,16,11); replay examples/hollow-actions.json; plan 'Three morning pours' stays {day:2, remaining:3, status:pending} while examples/lantern-hollow.json shows day 8 remaining 1. After fix the replay reproduces lantern-hollow.json workbench exactly.

provisional_claims.summary: Daily nutrient accounting: bare-ground +1 recovery was applied to planted tiles before the upkeep check, and the severe-strain nutrient return used pre-day vitality. Now +1 only for empty ground and strain return uses the day's vitality; engine reproduces examples/first-garden.json exactly.
provisional_claims.reproduction: create(34,16,11); step(w,24) vs examples/first-garden.json cells: 17 diffs (journal glowcap count differed) before; 0 diffs after.

provisional_claims.summary: Server/CLI defects: publish() replaced the current world before saving (save failure lost prior garden) and pushed the new trial instead of the prior garden onto undo; undo stack kept the oldest 30 instead of newest 30; new edits after undo did not clear redo branch; undo/redo reused snapshot revision+1 (not fresh revisions, stale revisions accepted); revision check accepted future/boolean revisions; legacy import without revision was re-numbered (checked "world" instead of "revision"); CLI errors exited 1 instead of documented 2; forecast same-path check compared raw strings.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Start GardenServer with save_path in unwritable dir -> POST /api/command returned 500 but world changed; after a command, POST /api/undo restored the edited garden rather than the original; 31 edits then undo returned oldest; `mosslight grow missing.json` exit 1 (doc says 2); `forecast g.json -o ./g.json` overwrote source.

provisional_claims.summary: execute() double-incremented revisions (mutators bump revision, then execute added +1 on top). A command is now exactly one revision: trial.revision = world.revision + 1. Replay of hollow-actions yields revision 16 as in examples/lantern-hollow.json.
provisional_claims.reproduction: replay(create(34,16,11), hollow-actions.json) -> revision 38 before, 16 after (reference save has 16).

provisional_claims.summary: field_calibration.estimate: least-squares spread/covariance computed from raw uncentered timestamps (sum t^2 - (sum t)^2/n), catastrophically cancelling for realistic epoch timestamps with fractional seconds, giving wrong/zero slopes; also duplicate timestamps were not averaged before fitting as documented. Now groups readings by timestamp (averaging) and fits on centered offsets.
provisional_claims.reproduction: b=1.7e9+0.25; estimate([{'timestamp':b,'moisture':40},{'timestamp':b+0.5,'moisture':41},{'timestamp':b+1,'moisture':42}], b+2) should be 44.0; old code produced a garbage slope due to cancellation.

provisional_claims.summary: Campaign fixes: (1) runtime.execution_version always returned conservation-2, so classic-1 campaigns (and replays) ran with the wrong ecological release; now uses the recorded definition runtime id; (2) publish accepted stale workers (WHERE generation=? OR owner!=?), letting a reclaimed/expired worker overwrite progress — now requires matching generation AND owner; (3) publish committed branch progress before writing its checkpoint/report in a second transaction, breaking atomic durable progress — now one transaction; (4) fork re-applied interventions at the checkpoint offset (already part of the checkpoint garden) as child offset 0 — now only events after the checkpoint; (5) compact computed descendant-origin checkpoints but deleted them anyway, breaking provenance of existing forks — protected checkpoints are now kept.
provisional_claims.reproduction: CampaignStore(db).create(world,6,treatments,2,'classic-1') with a rain_barrel: steps used conservation-2 barrel_adjustment. fork(c,1,2) with event at offset 2 included it again at child offset 0 (double watering). fork at offset 3 then compact(c,5) deleted checkpoint (1,3) so provenance(child) raised 'Checkpoint is unavailable'. Two claims with expired lease: first (stale) worker's publish still accepted.

provisional_claims.summary: Irrigation: (1) irrigation_flow.allocate skipped residual reverse arcs during augmentation, so it did not deliver the maximum flow the pipes permit (e.g., s->a->{t1,t2}, s->b->t1 delivered 1 instead of 2); (2) irrigation.solve merged candidate states by aggregate census rather than full garden state, discarding distinct gardens whose later outcomes differ, so the chosen schedule could be suboptimal over the full period.
provisional_claims.reproduction: allocate([s->a 1, a->t1 1, a->t2 1, s->b 1, b->t1 1],'s',{'t1':1,'t2':1},5) returned total 1; now 2. For solve: two choices watering different outlet tiles with identical census after day 1 were collapsed, losing the branch that wins on day 2.

provisional_claims.summary: Workspace catalog format-1 upgrade rebuilt the label index with the old (casefold-only) key function before installing the NFKC/whitespace key, so after upgrade searches miss existing receipts (even exact labels). Now installs the current key before REINDEX.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Create a format-1 catalog DB (catalog_format version 1, index on catalog_key(label) with casefold) containing label 'Field  Pond'; open with WorkspaceCatalog; search('field pond') and search('Field  Pond') both returned [] before; now return the receipt (also fullwidth query).

provisional_claims.summary: History fixes: (1) replay cache key only hashed the last event (events[-1:]), so a corrected/rebased history sharing a final event reused a stale checkpoint from a different prefix — key now covers the whole prefix; (2) replay resolved references using the author's original numeric binding instead of the logical entity's current local ID, so after a correction renumbered objects later actions edited the wrong object; (3) rebase used the parent's current head as merge base instead of the fork's recorded base_revision (parent changes after fork were treated as local deletions/conflicts); (4) cherry-pick identified shared actions by command content, merging independently authored identical actions — now by event identity; (5) rebase order check only considered the target's order, never detecting incompatible local orders — now respects both; (6) correct() canonicalized replacement numeric IDs against the final garden instead of the garden at that point in history.
provisional_claims.reproduction: create; append note A, note B, edit_note ident 2; correct({A_event: None}) -> B now has local id 1 but edit_note replayed with ident 2 (missing/wrong). fork; append to parent; rebase(fork, parent) used parent's new head as base so parent's new events were treated as removed. cherry_pick of a note identical to an existing target note was silently dropped.

provisional_claims.summary: History exchange: reconciliation's _common_bases truncated the set of maximal common ancestors to one (maximal[:1]). After criss-cross rounds (both collaborators reconciled the same work separately), only one merge base was used, so changes/reversions present in the other base were misattributed; the recursive comparison() over all maximal bases is now used as designed.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Two installations reconcile the same pair a1,b1 separately (m1, m2), then each edits (a2 from m1, b2 from m2); reconcile(a2,b2) computed common bases {a1,b1} but only used a1, so b1's authored work was treated as independent insertions/edits, dropping reversions or yielding spurious concurrent-edit conflicts.

provisional_claims.summary: Courier CRDT defects: (1) precedes() iterated the other clock's peers, so any event looked superseded by an event with empty/unrelated context (concurrent puts vanished); (2) _covered used the union of every record's context, so a selection or compaction for one observation deleted other observations' events on merge; (3) project() kept all records' contexts and the full clock, so merging a selection dropped observations it did not include and implied unseen edits/deletions; (4) concurrent edit+delete hid the observation (any vs all); (5) conflicting values differing only in case were collapsed (casefold); (6) acknowledged() used max instead of progress seen by every named device (min, missing ack = 0); (7) merge only compared the record when detecting reuse of a writer's event identity; (8) merged packet counter could lag its own writer's clock, causing dot reuse; (9) put stored caller-owned values by reference.
provisional_claims.reproduction: A=new_packet('x');B=new_packet('y');put(A,'k',{'text':'Fern'});put(B,'k',{'text':'fern'});observations(merge(A,B)) -> previously []/collapsed, now conflict ['Fern','fern']. A has r1,r2, B=merge(new_packet('b'),A); remove(A,'r2'); A=checkpoint(A); merge(B, project(A,['r1'])) previously lost r2; now r2 kept. acknowledged({'p':{'a':3},'q':{'a':1}},['p','q']) -> {'a':1}. remove vs concurrent put -> observation stays visible.

provisional_claims.summary: Ensemble fixes: (1) report(revision) replaced the archived result with a fresh summary of current outcomes, so published reports for earlier revisions changed after edits — now returns the archived envelope; (2) publish validated only the node's previous reads (empty for never-computed nodes), so a trial computed from inputs edited mid-flight was accepted with stale inputs — now validates the reads actually used; (3) ensemble_compute took the trial identity from a cache hit's origin, so two sources with equal saves (or shared plans) were reported under another replicate/treatment label — identity now always the requested one; (4) ensemble_reports paired controls by dict order via zip, misaligning treatment rows with other gardens' controls whenever a replicate was excluded — now pairs by replicate.
provisional_claims.reproduction: create ensemble with two equal source saves 'a','b'; work -> second node cache hit reported identity replicate 'a' twice, 'b' excluded. Edit plan after revision 0 published; report(e,0)['result'] changed to revision-1 outcomes. prepare ticket, edit source, publish ticket -> accepted with old source.

provisional_claims.summary: save_merge._logical_id mapped every record to ["base", id] regardless of origin, so records independently created on both replicas with the same local id were merged/conflicted as if one inherited record (docs: independently created records stay separate and get unique local ids). Now non-inherited ids are keyed by replica origin.
provisional_claims.reproduction: base with note 1; left add_note('left new') and right add_note('right new') (both id 2); reconcile(...) previously returned a conflict on /records/notes/["base",2]/text; now ready with notes 1,3,4 and allocation {"desk",2}->3, {"field",2}->4; verify_receipt True.

provisional_claims.summary: Study fixes: (1) later stages seeded every promoted treatment's job from the control's checkpoint, discarding the treatment's earlier care (continuations didn't extend the same experiment) — now continues from each treatment's own checkpoint; (2) stage decision was finalized as soon as any single garden had complete control+treatments, so worker completion order decided promotions on a partial cohort — decision now waits until all stage trials are terminal (complete/failed).
provisional_claims.reproduction: examples/study.json: after stage 0, stage-1 'Water' job state equaled control's state (no watering applied, parent anchor treatment 'control'). With two sources, run work_once in an order finishing 'north' first: report(stage 0) was saved with cohort common=['north'] only and 'south' excluded while its jobs were still pending.

provisional_claims.summary: Courier causal contexts leaked across observations: new events took the packet-wide clock as context and checkpoint stamped the global clock onto every record, so after merging a project()ed selection an edit/removal of an unrelated observation superseded (or a checkpoint later dropped) events the writer never saw. Events now carry the record's own clock (record_clock), checkpoint contexts use record_clock, and merge coverage uses record_clock.
provisional_claims.reproduction: p2 puts r3 {text:a}; p2 puts r1; p1 merges project(p2,['r1']); p1 remove(r3); p2 merges project(p1,['r3']) -> r3 disappears from p2 although p1 never saw p2's r3 put (should stay visible as concurrent edit/delete). Randomized reference-model test (tests/_courier_prop.py: puts/removes/merges/projections/checkpoints across 3-4 peers) went from ~130/300 failing seeds to 0.

provisional_claims.summary: Loaded gardens shared mutable state with the caller's save data: state.validate did state.update(raw.copy()) (shallow; unused `import copy` shows intended deepcopy), so notes/plans/tiles lists in a World created by World.from_dict were the same objects as the input dict (and tag normalization mutated the caller's input); model.from_dict likewise kept the input journal entry dicts. Now both deep-copy so a loaded World is independent of the supplied save representation.
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=create(1,5,5); add_note(w,'x',['A']); d=w.to_dict(); w2=World.from_dict(d); d['workbench']['notes'].clear() -> len(w2.workbench['notes']) was 0 (expected 1). Also from_dict with note tags ['B','A'] rewrote the caller's dict tags to ['a','b'].

provisional_claims.summary: Save validation: identifier uniqueness was reset per collection (inner ids=set()), so a save could reuse one id in notes and tasks even though ids come from one shared next_id counter and save merge/histories rely on globally unique identities; history day order accepted duplicate days (daily census records must strictly increase).
provisional_claims.reproduction: save with notes [{id:1}] and tasks [{id:1}] and next_id 3 -> World.from_dict accepted (now rejected: "Identifiers must be unique"); workbench history [{day:3},{day:3}] accepted (now rejected).

provisional_claims.summary: Harvest did not start a new growth period: it only subtracted 5 days of age (max(0, age-5)), so any plant older than harvest_age+5 could be harvested again immediately and repeatedly the same day. Docs: "Harvesting takes vigor and starts a new growth period before the next harvest" (and seed collection "likewise" resets age to 0). Harvest now resets the plant's growth age to 0, so the next harvest requires the species' harvest age again.
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=create(1,6,6); act(w,0,0,'plant_fern'); c=w.cell(0,0); c.age=30; c.vitality=90; harvest(w,0,0); harvest(w,0,0) -> second harvest succeeded immediately (age 25 >= 12). After fix the second call raises 'Harvest needs age 12'.

provisional_claims.summary: save_merge accepted any original with a matching seed/canvas as the common ancestor (docs: a matching seed or size alone is insufficient). Reconcile now rejects replicas dated before the supplied original or whose retained daily history diverges from the original's history for days up to the original's date. Also World.index accepted booleans as coordinates (isinstance) while all validators require true integers.
provisional_claims.reproduction: base=create(3,6,5) stepped 4 days + note; right = independently created create(3,6,5) stepped 2 days + note -> previously merged 'ready' mixing unrelated gardens; now ValueError. execute(w,{'op':'tend','args':{'x':True,'y':0,'action':'water'}}) previously watered tile (1,0); now rejected.

provisional_claims.summary: Save validation accepted journals of up to 200 events although the garden journal retains only 100 events (engine.log trims to the last 100; README: "the journal retains 100 events"). Oversized journals from edited/foreign saves were accepted as consistent data. Validation now rejects journals longer than 100 entries, matching the history (240) and collection (500) limits that already mirror the documented retention.
provisional_claims.reproduction: d=create(1,5,5).to_dict(); d['journal']=[{'day':0,'text':'x'}]*150; World.from_dict(d) was accepted (expected ValueError: Invalid journal).

provisional_claims.summary: field_calibration.estimate accepted non-numeric readings by coercing with float(): string timestamps/moisture ('0', '42'), booleans (True→1.0) and malformed rows (missing keys → KeyError, huge ints → OverflowError) instead of the documented numeric timestamp/moisture requirement and clear ValueError. Readings and target time are now validated as real numbers (bool excluded) with a ValueError for malformed rows; valid inputs produce identical estimates.
provisional_claims.reproduction: estimate([{'timestamp':'0','moisture':'42'}], 1) returned 42.0 (expected ValueError); estimate([{'timestamp':True,'moisture':42}],1) accepted; estimate([{'moisture':4}],1) raised KeyError. Doc example still returns 43.5.

provisional_claims.summary: Campaign fork from the initial checkpoint (offset -1, retained by compaction) shifted every inherited intervention one day late and ran one extra day (days = parent_days - (-1), child offset = event_offset + 1), so the continuation diverged from the parent's timeline. Fork now anchors relative dates at max(offset, 0), so a fork at the start reproduces the parent branch and forks at later checkpoints are unchanged.
provisional_claims.reproduction: c=create(first-garden, 6, treatments.json, 2); run to completion; f=fork(c,2,-1); run; previously f ran 7 days with 'Extra water' at child offsets 2 and 5 (final census differed from parent branch 2); now final census equals parent branch 2 and control equals parent control.

provisional_claims.summary: Propagation bench: hydrated days only improved vigor while a batch was still 'growing'; once 'ready', a watered batch consumed water but never regained vigor (the +3 was conditioned on status). Docs: "A batch needs regular watering even after it is ready ... Hydrated days develop the batch and improve its vigor; dry days halt development and weaken it." Hydrated days now add vigor (capped at 100) for any living batch.
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=create(1,6,6); w.workbench['seeds']['clover']=1; b=start_seeds(w,'clover'); step(w,2) -> ready; water_batch(w,b['id']); v=batch vitality; step(w,1) -> vitality unchanged (expected v+3).

provisional_claims.summary: Analysis: (1) transect used a non-standard Bresenham step test (error*2 > dy instead of >=), so steep lines took the axis step at exact ties and were not the transpose of the equivalent shallow line (0,0)->(1,2) gave (0,1) instead of (1,1)); (2) patch survey listed patches smallest-first; patches are now ranked largest-first with top-left position breaking ties.
provisional_claims.reproduction: transect(w,0,0,1,2) -> [(0,0),(0,1),(1,2)] while transect(w,0,0,2,1) -> [(0,0),(1,1),(2,1)]; now steep case gives [(0,0),(1,1),(1,2)]. patches(w) on a garden with patch sizes 1 and 5 returned [1,...,5]; now largest first.
